LESSON: POETRY 9.2.1 APPRECIATION OF POETRY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Poetry 9.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Poetry 9.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry, part of Strand 9 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to study a variety of themes in poetry?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the mood and tone in a poem for literary appreciation,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Poetry 9.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. examine the subject matter in poems for literary analysis,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Poetry 9.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. analyse themes in a variety of poems for literary appreciation,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Poetry 9.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. acknowledge the significance of subject matter in poems for literary appreciation.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Poetry 9.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify the mood and tone in a poem for literary appreciation,

   Poetry 9.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. examine the subject matter in poems for literary analysis,

   Poetry 9.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. analyse themes in a variety of poems for literary appreciation,

   Poetry 9.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. acknowledge the significance of subject matter in poems for literary appreciation.

   Poetry 9.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. identify the persona in the poem,

2. discuss the tone and mood of the poem and make notes,

3. brainstorm on the subject matter in poems from Kenya and share with peers,

4. read a variety of poems and collaborate to describe the subject matter,

5. search a variety of poems from Kenya on different themes and discuss them in class with peers,

6. recite poems on the environment and analyse their themes,

7. share findings with peers,

8. discuss the significance of the subject matter in poems,

9. conduct poetry sessions as a class to read varied poems from Kenya,

10. prepare a reading log on poems read and identify the subject matter and themes from the poems,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. identify the persona in the poem,
2. discuss the tone and mood of the poem and make notes,
3. brainstorm on the subject matter in poems from Kenya and share with peers,
4. read a variety of poems and collaborate to describe the subject matter,
5. search a variety of poems from Kenya on different themes and discuss them in class with peers,
6. recite poems on the environment and analyse their themes,
7. share findings with peers,
8. discuss the significance of the subject matter in poems,
9. conduct poetry sessions as a class to read varied poems from Kenya,
10. prepare a reading log on poems read and identify the subject matter and themes from the poems,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Poetry 9.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: This is enhanced as the learner exhibits self-drive as they conduct poetry sessions as a class to read varied

poems from Kenya.

● Learning to learn: This is inculcated as the learner builds on their learning experiences by sharing their reading logs with

peers for peer reviews and recommendations.

Values:
Unity: This is nurtured as the learner collaborate to brainstorms on subject matter in poetry and shares with peers harmoniously.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship Education: This is developed as the learner searches a variety of poems from Kenya on different themes and

discusses them in class with peers.

Inquiry Question(s)

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify the mood and tone in a poem for literary appreciation,
2. examine the subject matter in poems for literary analysis,
3. analyse themes in a variety of poems for literary appreciation,
4. acknowledge the significance of subject matter in poems for literary appreciation.

Remember the key question: Why is it important to study a variety of themes in poetry?
